analysis_note: Rules-only deterministic audit of graph vs text verification on the frozen membud-evaluation-v2 manifest (36 synthetic cases, 10 expected-invalid). No paid model calls were made and gold labels were used only for reporting. Information parity: plain text sees the claim sets but not evidence.contradicts; graph and the fair-text control both see contradiction annotations. Therefore text-vs-text_fair differences isolate the value of contradiction access, while text_fair-vs-graph differences isolate verifier construction. Adding contradiction access changes decisions on DEV-13, HELD-13; plain text false-accepts DEV-13, HELD-13, fair text false-accepts no faulty cases. Fair text and graph agree on all 26 non-invalid cases. Conclusion: on this manifest, once contradiction information access is equalized, structural graph verification adds no decision-level detection power beyond the fair text control. The graph-vs-plain-text gap observed on contradiction cases is explained by information access, not by representation. This is narrow evidence from a small, single-reviewer, synthetic set and does not establish equivalence in general; it does mean the earlier graph advantage should not be attributed to graph structure. Limitations: 36 hand-authored synthetic Indonesian-themed cases, single-reviewer labels with second review pending, and rules-only verifiers. INVALID_INPUT rows are schema-construction failures recorded before verification, not verifier decisions.
